notes: This diagnostic contains only 24 baseline catalogue barcode-hit images. All are positive and all image digests are unique. It has no negatives or ordinary barcode-miss images.
Barcode retention is measured against these known baseline hits. It is not general image recognition recall or a corpus estimate.
These variants scan fresh crops only. They do not scan the whole image before or after a crop miss. The existing model pipeline handles the miss.
Missing detection means no crop was available. Available geometry with no accepted code means a decode miss, not a native decoder exception.
The records cannot determine whether a crop miss came from the rectangle, crop scale, image quality, or limited decode passes. No images were inspected.
The crop SAM3 request, sent-image preparation, geometry, and decode costs are inside the barcode stage and HTTP timing. Do not sum nested timers.
A later fallback package segmentation repeats SAM3. Crop responses are not reused.
Each variant uses one persistent backend. Its first request includes child startup and backend construction. Service setup is outside HTTP wall. Later rows have zero incremental startup/build.
After-first does not establish warm remote models. The sample contains only one fallback rerank call.

HTTP covers loopback upload through complete response read, including steps_answer. Browser rendering, remote client LAN, source-file read, JSON parse, service setup, and final session worker shutdown are outside that timer.
All 72 observations remain in the denominators. There were no pending, failed, censored, or degraded responses. An incorrect HTTP200 response is still an identification failure.
Each variant ran once in fixed order. Sample quantiles are descriptive. No hard 3-second deadline is implemented or demonstrated.
